issues.display_title: Issue #566: Eliminate Redundant Panorama Upload Pipelines & Stream Direct-to-Disk Downloads
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Eliminate Redundant Panorama Upload Pipelines & Stream Direct-to-Disk Downloads

  • Date: 2026-10-27
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Configuration: ZERO NEW ENV REQUIRED

1. Summary

Refactored the panorama upload pipeline across UploadPanoramaPost.go, UploadPanoramaGDrive.go, UploadPanoramaDbx.go, AddPostGothru.go, and cloud_storage.go:

  1. Centralized Quota & Post Ownership Check:

    • Implemented CheckMultiplePostQuota with typed struct mapping (Take(&res)).
    • Replaced untyped map[string]interface{} scanning and duplicated query boilerplate.

  2. Centralized MinIO/S3 Storage Upload:

    • Implemented UploadFileToStorage handling client initialization, bucket creation, upload, and automatic local file cleanup on failure.

  3. Centralized ImageProxy Signing & URL Generation:

    • Implemented GeneratePanoramaURLs replacing 15 copy-pasted lines with a single function call.

  4. Centralized Location Input Parsing:

    • Implemented ParseLocationInput removing duplicate unmarshalling blocks.

  5. Streaming Direct-to-Disk Download:

    • Replaced memory-heavy io.ReadAll in DownloadDropbox with io.Copy(outFile, content) to prevent OOM crashes on high-res panorama downloads.

  6. Automated Testing:

    • Added unit test cases TestParseLocationInput_Empty, TestParseLocationInput_Valid, TestCheckMultiplePostQuota_NilDB, and TestGeneratePanoramaURLs_DefaultSigning in post_upload_helpers_test.go.

2. Files Modified & Created

  • Modified:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_upload_helpers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_upload_helpers_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadPanoramaPost.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadPanoramaGDrive.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadPanoramaDbx.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostGothru.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/cloud_storage.go
  • Created:
    • docs/tasks/2026-10-27/eliminate_redundant_panorama_upload_pipeline.md
    • docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-27/eliminate_redundant_panorama_upload_pipeline_impl.md

3. Verification

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Posts
# PASS (100% passed in 0.203s)

go vet ./src/...
# PASS (0 warnings)

go build ./cmd/...
# PASS (0 errors)
  • Area: Posts / Upload / Panorama / Storage / Code Redundancy / Memory Safety
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_upload_helpers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_upload_helpers_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadPanoramaPost.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadPanoramaGDrive.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UploadPanoramaDbx.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostGothru.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/cloud_storage.go
  • Date: 2026-10-27

1. Problem & Context

Multiple panorama upload endpoints (UploadPanoramaPost, UploadPanoramaGDrive, UploadPanoramaDbx, and AddPostGothru) contained over 150 lines of duplicate copy-pasted code:

  1. Redundant Quota Verification:
    • Querying views_total_multiple_posts and validating ValidateMultiplePostQuota(totalMult, 10) was duplicated verbatim across 3 files using untyped []map[string]interface{} scanning.
  2. Duplicate MinIO Upload & Error Cleanup:
    • Connecting to MinIO client, bucket creation, uploading, and deleting the local file on error was duplicated across 4 files.
  3. Duplicate ImageProxy URL Generation:
    • Reading IMG_KEY/IMG_SALT from environment, hex-decoding signing secrets, formatting s3://%s/%s, and generating multiple resolution URLs was copy-pasted 5 times.
  4. Duplicate Location Parsing:
    • Unmarshalling location JSON and extracting locationPost and locationName was repeated 3 times.
  5. Memory Safety (OOM):
    • DownloadDropbox in cloud_storage.go used io.ReadAll(content) into RAM, risking OOM crashes for large panorama files.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Unified Helper Pipeline (post_upload_helpers.go):
    • CheckMultiplePostQuota(userId, sid, qSid string, maxQuota int64) (string, error) with strongly-typed struct scanning.
    • UploadFileToStorage(bucket, filename, localPath, contentType string) error encapsulating MinIO client creation, upload, and automatic local cleanup on error.
    • GeneratePanoramaURLs(encrypt, filename string, width, height int) (string, fiber.Map) consolidating environment decoding and URL creation into a single line.
    • ParseLocationInput(location string) (map[string]interface{}, *string, error).
  2. Streaming Direct-to-Disk (cloud_storage.go):
    • Replaced io.ReadAll in DownloadDropbox with io.Copy(outFile, content), keeping memory footprint at ~0 MB.
  3. Zero Configuration:
    • No new environment variables added; 100% backward-compatible.
  4. Unit Tests:
    • Added unit tests for new helpers in post_upload_helpers_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • Over 150 lines of duplicate code eliminated.
  • Panorama upload endpoints maintain identical behavior and HTTP contracts.
  • 100% unit tests pass cleanly in src/Action/V1/Posts.
  • Clean build and vet checks.

issues.display_title: Issue #567: Centralize Cryptographically Secure OTP Generation & Eliminate Duplicate Upsert Pipelines
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Cryptographically Secure OTP Generation & Eliminate Duplicate Upsert Pipelines

  • Date: 2026-10-27
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Configuration: ZERO NEW ENV REQUIRED

1. Summary

Secured and deduplicated OTP generation and storage across Users and Auth packages:

  1. CWE-338 Hardening via crypto/rand:

    • Implemented GenerateSecure4DigitOTP() and GenerateSecure6DigitOTP() in src/Utils/Functions/crypto.go.
    • Replaced predictable math/rand.Intn(...) in ResendOtp.go, ForgotPassword.go, OtpDelete.go, and Login.go.
    • Replaced custom OTP generation in MagicLink.go.

  2. Deduplication of Database Upsert & Email Queueing:

    • Implemented UserFunctions.UpsertOtpRecord and UserFunctions.SendOtpEmailQueue in src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go.
    • Delegated UpsertUserOtp in Users/otp_helpers.go and UpsertEmailVerificationOtp in Auth/helpers.go to the centralized implementation.
    • Removed 60+ lines of duplicated GORM SQL and RabbitMQ publishing logic.

  3. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Added TestGenerateSecure4DigitOTP and TestGenerateSecure6DigitOTP in src/Utils/Functions/otp_test.go.
    • Added TestUpsertOtpRecord_NilDB in src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions_test.go.

3. Verification

# PASS (100% tests passed)

go vet ./src/...
# PASS (0 warnings)

go build ./cmd/...
# PASS (0 errors)
  • Area: Auth / Users / Security / OTP / Redundancy Elimination
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Utils/Functions/crypto.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/otp_test.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/otp_helpers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ResendOtp.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ForgotPassword.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/OtpDelete.go
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/Login.go
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink.go
  • Date: 2026-10-27

1. Problem & Context

  1. Insecure Pseudo-Random Number Generation (CWE-338):
    • In 4 separate handlers (ResendOtp.go, ForgotPassword.go, OtpDelete.go, Login.go), 4-digit OTP codes were generated using math/rand:
      otpCode := rand.Intn(9000) + 1000
    • math/rand generates predictable sequences, presenting a severe account takeover and credential compromise risk.
  2. Duplicate OTP Database Upsert Logic:
    • Both Users/otp_helpers.go (UpsertUserOtp) and Auth/helpers.go (UpsertEmailVerificationOtp) duplicated identical SQL queries on Models.Otp (user_id = ? AND type = ?), inserting or updating the verification code and expiration time.
  3. Duplicate Email Queue Construction:
    • Constructing email payloads for verification, forgot password, and delete account was repeated across several files.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Cryptographically Secure OTP Generators (src/Utils/Functions/crypto.go):
    • Added GenerateSecure4DigitOTP() (1000 - 9999) using crypto/rand.
    • Added GenerateSecure6DigitOTP() (100000 - 999999) using crypto/rand.
    • Updated ResendOtp, ForgotPassword, OtpDelete, Login, and MagicLink to use secure generators.
  2. Centralized OTP Storage Pipeline (src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go):
    • Created UpsertOtpRecord(userId uuid.UUID, subject string, otpCode int, expiredAt time.Time) error.
    • Created SendOtpEmailQueue(toEmail, fullname, subject, template string, otpCode int, logPath string, logBody []byte) error.
    • Refactored Users/otp_helpers.go and Auth/helpers.go to delegate directly to these shared functions, eliminating 60+ lines of duplicate database and queue logic.
  3. Zero Configuration:
    • No new environment variables required.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added TestGenerateSecure4DigitOTP, TestGenerateSecure6DigitOTP, and TestUpsertOtpRecord_NilDB.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • All OTP generation uses crypto/rand.
  • Duplicate database upsert queries for OTP are eliminated.
  • 100% of unit tests pass in Users, Auth, and Functions.
  • Clean build and vet checks.

1. Problem & Context

Across 20+ endpoint handlers in panorra-api-go-new, returning either plain JSON or encrypted payload (ec == "true") repeated this identical 9-line boilerplate:

if ec == "true" {
    encText, _ := Functions.EncryptResponse(response, lastLogin, encrypt)
    return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(fiber.Map{
        "cry": encText,
        "ls":  Functions.EpochTime(lastLogin),
    })
}
return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(response)

This resulted in over 150+ lines of duplicate boilerplate. Any modification to the encrypted envelope structure required editing dozens of files individually.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Centralized Response Dispatcher (src/Utils/Functions/response.go):
    • Implemented SendJSONOrEncrypted(c *fiber.Ctx, response interface{}, lastLogin, encrypt string, shouldEncrypt bool, extras ...fiber.Map) error.
    • Encapsulates encryption, epoch calculation, status code dispatching, and optional extra field injection.
  2. Refactored Handlers:
    • Replaced repeated 9-line blocks across 12+ files with a clean one-liner:
      return Functions.SendJSONOrEncrypted(c, response, lastLogin, encrypt, ec == "true")
    • Preserved optional custom envelope fields (e.g. message, e4) using variadic extras.
  3. Zero Configuration:
    • No new environment variables needed.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added TestSendJSONOrEncrypted_PlainJSON and TestSendJSONOrEncrypted_EncryptedWithExtras in response_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • Identical response envelope structure and encryption semantics preserved.
  • 150+ lines of boilerplate eliminated.
  • 100% of unit tests pass cleanly across Posts, Users, Bookmarks, CollectionPost, and Functions.
  • Clean build and vet checks.

issues.display_title: Issue #569: Exhaustive Redis Nil-Pointer Defense and Graceful Degradation
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Exhaustive Redis Nil-Pointer Defense and Graceful Degradation

  • Date: 2026-10-27
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Comprehensive audit and remediation of all raw RedisClient invocations across panorra-api-go-new and panorra-api-go:

  1. Panorama Cache Nil Defense:
    • Protected 14 methods in src/Utils/Redis/panorama_cache.go to return safe defaults ("", 0, false, nil, or empty slice/map) without crashing when Redis is nil.
  2. Post Cache & Scanner Nil Defense:
    • Added guards to scanKeys, ListBookmarksUser, ReplaceBlockedPostEC, and ReplaceEmbedPost in src/Utils/Redis/post_cache.go and client.go.

  3. Background Job & Worker Protection:

    • Protected InsertViewPost.go, SetAllListUserOnRedis.go, and DeleteUser.go.
    • Protected UpdatePostVisibility.go and ProgressBannedUser.go.
  4. Cross-Repo Hardening:
    • Protected ListCategories.go in panorra-api-go against nil Redis and nil Config.DB.
  5. Automated Unit Testing:

    • panorra-api-go-new/src/Worker/UpdatePostVisibility/UpdatePostVisibility.go
    • panorra-api-go-new/src/Worker/BannedUser/ProgressBannedUser.go

    • panorra-api-go/src/Action/V1/Categories/ListCategories_test.go
  • Date: 2026-10-27

1. Problem & Context

Across panorra-api-go-new and panorra-api-go, multiple cache helpers and controllers called RedisClient methods (Get, Set, Del, Incr, Scan, SetNX, Exists) without checking whether RedisClient was initialized or connected:

  1. Nil Pointer Panic Hazard:
    • If Redis went down, restarted, or was in the middle of a reconnection cycle (RedisClient == nil), calling any of these functions immediately triggered a fatal SIGSEGV runtime panic, aborting HTTP request handler goroutines.
  2. Lack of Graceful Degradation:
    • Instead of falling back to database queries (e.g., in ListEmbedPost, InsertViewPost, ListCategories), the service crashed.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Exhaustive Guarding in panorama_cache.go:
    • Guarded all 14 functions (SetPanoramaStatus, GetPanoramaStatus, DeletePanoramaStatus, GetRequeueStatus, IncrementRequeueStatus, DeleteRequeueStatus, InitializeRequeueStatus, DeleteAllPanoramaStatus, SavePostCompletePayload, GetPostCompletePayload, DeletePostCompletePayload, CheckAllPanoramaReady, TryAcquirePostCompleteTrigger, DeletePostCompleteTriggerLock) returning safe zero values or fallback allowances when RedisClient == nil.
  2. Exhaustive Guarding in post_cache.go and client.go:
    • Guarded scanKeys, ListBookmarksUser, ReplaceBlockedPostEC, ReplaceEmbedPost, and ListEmbedPost.
  3. Guards in Handlers and Workers:
    • InsertViewPost.go: Guarded redis.Get on deactivated users.
    • SetAllListUserOnRedis.go & DeleteUser.go: Guarded redis.Set.
    • UpdatePostVisibility.go: Guarded ListBookmarksUser.
    • ProgressBannedUser.go: Guarded user-details cache flush.
    • ListCategories.go (in panorra-api-go): Guarded redis.Get, redis.Set, and Config.DB.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added TestPanoramaCache_NilRedisClient_NoPanics in client_test.go and TestListCategories_NilRedisDoesNotPanic in ListCategories_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • All Redis methods safely degrade without throwing nil-pointer panics when Redis is uninitialized or disconnected.
  • 100% unit tests pass across both repositories.
  • Zero new environment variables required.

issues.display_title: Issue #570: MinIO S3 Operations Context Timeout and Anti-Hang Bounding
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: MinIO S3 Operations Context Timeout and Anti-Hang Bounding

  • Date: 2026-10-27
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Configuration: ZERO NEW ENV REQUIRED

1. Summary

Bound all storage operations in src/Utils/Minio/MinioFunctions.go to context deadlines with production-tuned headroom:

  1. Context-Bounded Operations with Tuned Headroom:

    • Replaced unbounded context.Background() with scoped timeouts:
      • DefaultBucketTimeout = 15 * time.Second
      • DefaultUploadTimeout = 180 * time.Second (3 minutes) — prevents premature timeouts on 100MB+ 8K/12K panorama files while eliminating permanent hangs.
      • DefaultDeleteTimeout = 60 * time.Second (1 minute) — provides sufficient time to recursively delete multi-resolution tile folders.

  2. Context-Aware Method Hierarchy:

    • Implemented CheckBucketWithContext, CreateBucketWithContext, UploadFileAwsWithContext, DeleteFileAwsWithContext, and DeleteBucketWithContext.
    • Backward-compatible standard functions (CheckBucket, CreateBucket, UploadFileAws, DeleteFileAws, DeleteBucket) forward to context methods with scoped deadlines.

  3. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Added TestMinioTimeoutsHaveValidDeadlines in MinioFunctions_test.go verifying timeout constants and context deadline properties.

2. Files Modified & Created

  • Modified:
    • src/Utils/Minio/MinioFunctions.go
    • src/Utils/Minio/MinioFunctions_test.go
  • Created:
    • docs/tasks/2026-10-27/minio_s3_context_timeout.md
    • docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-27/minio_s3_context_timeout_impl.md

3. Verification

go test -v ./src/Utils/Minio/...
# PASS (100% tests passed)

go vet ./src/...
# PASS (0 warnings)

go build ./cmd/...
# PASS (0 errors)
  • Area: Infrastructure / Storage / MinIO / S3 / Anti-Hang / High Availability
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Utils/Minio/MinioFunctions.go
    • src/Utils/Minio/MinioFunctions_test.go
  • Date: 2026-10-27

1. Problem & Context

In src/Utils/Minio/MinioFunctions.go, all storage calls (BucketExists, MakeBucket, PutObject, RemoveObject, RemoveBucket, ListObjects) used unconstrained context.Background():

ctx := context.Background() // Unbounded!
_, err = minioClient.PutObject(ctx, ...)

If the MinIO or S3 endpoint experienced socket freezes, network partitions, or storage backend timeouts, HTTP request handlers and background panorama upload workers hung indefinitely, exhausting worker threads and memory.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Context-Bounded Operations with Realistic Headroom:
    • Introduced DefaultBucketTimeout = 15 * time.Second for bucket metadata operations (CheckBucket, CreateBucket).
    • Introduced DefaultUploadTimeout = 180 * time.Second (3 minutes) for file uploads (UploadFileAws), providing sufficient headroom for high-resolution 8K/12K panorama files (100MB+) over cross-region networks while preventing indefinite hangs.
    • Introduced DefaultDeleteTimeout = 60 * time.Second (1 minute) for object/bucket deletions (DeleteFileAws, DeleteBucket), ensuring plenty of time to recursively iterate and delete multi-resolution tiles.
  2. Context-Aware Signatures:
    • Added CheckBucketWithContext, CreateBucketWithContext, UploadFileAwsWithContext, DeleteFileAwsWithContext, and DeleteBucketWithContext allowing parent contexts to be passed when needed while standard methods automatically apply default timeout contexts.
    • 100% backward-compatible with all existing callers.
  3. Zero Configuration:
    • Purely internal constants; zero new environment variables required.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added TestMinioTimeoutsHaveValidDeadlines in MinioFunctions_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • Storage operations cannot hang indefinitely.
  • Large 100MB+ panorama uploads have generous 3-minute headroom.
  • Backward compatibility preserved for all MinIO callers.
  • 100% unit tests pass cleanly in src/Utils/Minio.
  • Clean build and vet checks.
